questions.stem: fetch('/api/x') resolves with a Response when:
choices: On any successful network round trip, regardless of HTTP status
Only when the body is valid JSON
questions.explanation: fetch only rejects on network errors. 4xx and 5xx still resolve; you must check response.ok or response.status.

questions.stem: In event delegation, attaching a single listener to a parent works because of:
choices: Bubbling — events propagate from target up to ancestors
questions.explanation: By default handlers fire on bubble. A click on a deep child reaches every ancestor listener unless someone calls stopPropagation.
Sync first (1, 4). Microtasks (Promise) run before macrotasks (setTimeout), so 3 before 2.

questions.stem: Which API is safer when inserting untrusted user input into the DOM?
questions.explanation: textContent treats the input as raw text and never parses tags or scripts, eliminating an XSS sink.

questions.stem: Which loop runs N fetches in parallel?
choices: for (const id of ids) await fetch(`/u/${id}`);
questions.explanation: Mapping to promises then Promise.all starts them all at once. The for-of with await is strictly sequential.

questions.stem: Inside a delegated handler, `e.target` refers to:
choices: The element the listener was attached to
The element that actually received the event
questions.explanation: e.target is the original target. e.currentTarget is the element the handler is bound to.

questions.stem: Promise.all rejects when:
questions.explanation: Promise.all short-circuits on the first rejection. Use Promise.allSettled to wait for every promise.
async functions always return a promise. Returning 1 resolves it to 1, which the .then receives.

questions.stem: Which selector returns a live HTMLCollection (auto-updating)?
questions.explanation: getElementsByClassName/TagName return live HTMLCollections that mutate with the DOM. querySelectorAll returns a static NodeList.

questions.stem: How do you cancel a fetch request?
choices: Use AbortController and pass its signal to fetch
questions.explanation: const c = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: c.signal }); c.abort(); is the standard pattern.

questions.stem: Which is true about `e.preventDefault()` vs `e.stopPropagation()`?
choices: They are aliases for each other
preventDefault cancels the default browser action; stopPropagation halts further capture/bubble
Both stop the event from being delivered to any handler
preventDefault only works on form submit
questions.explanation: Different jobs: prevent the browser doing its default (link nav, form submit) vs stop the event continuing through the tree.

questions.stem: Which is the safest way to set HTML from a string of trusted markup, but still get DOM efficiency?
questions.explanation: Build inside a DocumentFragment, then append once — single reflow. innerHTML += is the worst because it re-parses the whole subtree.

questions.stem: What does `await` do?
choices: Blocks the entire thread until the promise settles
Pauses the async function and yields control until the promise settles
Converts a value to a promise
Schedules a callback for the next tick
questions.explanation: await suspends only the async function's frame. The event loop continues to run other tasks.
await on a rejected promise throws inside the async context, which the surrounding try/catch handles.

questions.stem: An event listener attached with `{ capture: true }` runs:
choices: During the capture phase, before the target phase
questions.explanation: Capture listeners run on the way down from window to target — before any bubble listeners on descendants.

questions.stem: What is the difference between `el.classList.add('x')` and `el.className = 'x'`?
choices: classList.add appends to existing classes; setting className replaces them all
questions.explanation: classList is a token-aware API; className is the raw string and overwrites everything previously there.

questions.stem: Why call `e.target.closest('.item')` in a delegated handler?
choices: To find an ancestor (or the element itself) matching the selector
questions.explanation: closest walks up from the target to find the nearest matching element, so clicks on inner spans still resolve to the .item row.

questions.stem: Which fetch option sends cookies to a cross-origin request?
questions.explanation: Cross-origin fetch omits cookies by default. credentials: 'include' opts in; the server must also send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials.

questions.stem:
What is logged?

Promise.resolve(1).then(v => v + 1).then(v => console.log(v));
questions.explanation: Each .then receives the previous resolved value. 1 + 1 = 2 flows to the next then.

questions.stem: Which is the correct way to read a JSON response body?
questions.explanation: Response.json() is async because the body may stream. await res.json() gives you the parsed object.

questions.stem: Which is correct about innerHTML and XSS?
choices: Assigning user-controlled strings to innerHTML can execute scripts via tags like
innerHTML is safe if you trim whitespace
questions.explanation: innerHTML parses the string as HTML. Even though <script> tags inserted that way don't execute, attribute event handlers do.

questions.stem: What does Promise.allSettled return?
choices: An array of { status, value | reason } objects, one per input promise
questions.explanation: allSettled waits for every promise and gives you a per-input object describing whether it fulfilled or rejected and with what.

questions.stem: What problem does the 'sequence number guard' pattern solve in search-as-you-type?
choices: Out-of-order responses where a slow earlier request overwrites the latest results
questions.explanation: Without a guard, a late-returning earlier request can overwrite the most recent UI. A monotonic sequence id lets you discard stale responses.

questions.stem: Which DOM method runs a CSS selector and returns the FIRST match?
questions.explanation: querySelector takes a CSS selector and returns the first matching element or null.

questions.stem: An async function `f()` is called. What does `typeof f()` return?
questions.explanation: An async function returns a Promise, and typeof Promise is 'object'.
